A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EfficientQAT and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization, instruction-tuning, component-ablation, and efficiency results in Section 4, plus original vision-language experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds calibration-dataset results for Block-AP in Appendix F, Table 13.

M1.justification: Both versions use Block-AP to train weights, step sizes, and zero points block by block, followed by E2E-QP with fixed quantized weights and trainable step sizes. Quantization, reconstruction training, gradients, and instruction-tuning procedures are unchanged. The new discussion of inter-block interactions explains the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix F adds WikiText2 and C4 as Block-AP calibration/training corpora alongside RedPajama, introducing training conditions with different corpus distributions. These datasets previously appeared as evaluation datasets. The downstream benchmark suite and vision-language task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds ApiQ to Table 3, PB-LLM and DB-LLM to the Llama-2-7B comparison, and PB-LLM to the Llama-3-70B comparison in Table 2. Table 9 adds BitDistiller, PB-LLM, and DB-LLM to training-cost comparisons. Conversely, the QuIP# and AQLM inference-speed comparisons in v1 Figure 2a are removed.

E3.justification: The added calibration study compares Block-AP without E2E-QP at w3g128 and w2g64 across three training corpora. Expanded baseline comparisons also introduce additional model/group-size configurations, including group-64 OmniQ results. Existing EfficientQAT learning rates, training budgets, context lengths, evaluation harness, and MMLU protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a calibration-source sensitivity analysis in Appendix F, Table 13, examining perplexity and zero-shot accuracy after training Block-AP on WikiText2, C4, or RedPajama. The existing component, trainable-parameter, sample-count, and group-size ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional result rows continue the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Most scores are retained. Table 6 changes Block-AP average perplexity/accuracy from 8.65/58.94 to 8.53/58.99, and Table 3 changes OmniQ's Llama-2-70B w2g128 WikiText2 perplexity from 6.11 to 6.55. v2 adds calibration, baseline, and training-cost entries and removes Figure 2a's vector-method speed results. Its new Table 2 Llama-3-70B group-128 row reports perplexities 6.07/9.23, which Table 3 assigns to group 64; this inconsistency does not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The quantization/dequantization equations, E2E step-size derivative, STE gradient expressions, and average-bits formula are unchanged. The gradient appendix moves from C to B without changing its mathematics. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims Block-AP is the first method to train all parameters directly during block-wise reconstruction and argues that complex auxiliary trainable-parameter designs are unnecessary. The central two-stage efficiency and accuracy claims remain. The abstract also corrects the retained 69.48-versus-72.41 comparison from less than 3% degradation to less than 3 points.

C2.justification: v2 explains E2E-QP through inter-block interactions and attributes PEQA's weakness to limited trainable parameters rather than primarily poor initialization. Appendix F adds an interpretation of calibration-distribution effects and recommends diverse corpora. v1's limitations section is removed, including its explicit warning that comparable 4-bit PTQ results are obtained faster; Section 4.1 still acknowledges comparable 4-bit accuracy and Llama-3 degradation.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds ApiQ result provenance. Section 4.4 documents additional comparator GPU requirements and names T-MAC and Marlin as deployment options. EfficientQAT's code link, core hyperparameters, and implementation disclosures remain unchanged. The new reproducibility statement mainly points to information already present.

R1.justification: v2 sharpens the novelty positioning against OmniQuant, AutoRound, BRECQ, and CBQ through its explicit first-method claim. It adds references including ApiQ, T-MAC, and Marlin and removes citations including QuIP, TEQ, Norm Tweaking, and the original Llama paper. The principal related-work categories and closest-method comparison with PEQA remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and much of the introduction are substantially rewritten around optimization freedom and inter-block interactions. The appendix opening is reorganized with an overview and reproducibility statement, while the limitations and broader-impact sections disappear. Citation style, author information, and efficiency prose also change, although much of the method and experiment text is retained.

P2.justification: v2 combines the retained accuracy, instruction-tuning, and training-time plots into a three-panel Figure 1 and removes the inference-speed panel. It adds training-cost and calibration tables, expands Tables 2–3, and relocates v1 Table 9 to Appendix C as Table 10. Headers, typography, and placement change, while most retained displays preserve their structure.

improvement.justification: The calibration-source study and additional baselines provide useful validation, and the Table 6 revision resolves its discrepancy with Table 5. However, v2 removes the explicit faster-PTQ limitation and direct vector-quantization speed evidence, while introducing a group-size/perplexity inconsistency in Table 2. The added evidence improves breadth, but qualification and numerical consistency weaken in specific places; these opposing effects prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
